data_output.description: Unchanged interface from data.py: load returns canonical date-filtered train, valid, and test source-row sequences; test labels are withheld when include_test_labels=False. encode returns encoded[split] = (features, labels, users), with features shaped (N, 5) and ordered as [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday]. Raw fields are exactly user_id, video_id, tab, hourmin, and date; hour is floor(numeric hourmin / 100) constrained to 0..23, and weekday is the Monday=0 through Sunday=6 calendar weekday from YYYYMMDD date. Validation and test prediction row order is this unchanged encoded split order.

model_input.description: Unchanged Model interface: Model.step receives aligned nonempty positive_features and negative_features arrays of equal shape (pair_count, 5). train.py must construct these by indexing training features with aligned int64 positive_indices and negative_indices. For each eligible training positive, build up to four pairs against distinct same-user training negatives, uniformly sampled without replacement when at least four negatives exist; otherwise use all available same-user negatives once. Model.predict receives a (N, 5) feature matrix and returns one score per input row.

trainer.objective: Implement the exact K=4 same-user-negative sampling ablation in train.py only, so every eligible positive training row contributes up to four distinct same-user negative comparisons per epoch.
required_changes: In train.py, change build_train_pairs so that for each user group with at least one train_labels[index] == 1 and at least one train_labels[index] == 0, each positive index is paired with K=4 negative indices sampled uniformly without replacement from that same group's negative index list when the group has at least four negatives.

When a user group has fewer than four negatives, pair each eligible positive with every available same-user negative exactly once; do not sample with replacement and do not duplicate a negative for the same positive in an epoch.

Append the positive index once for each sampled negative and append the corresponding sampled negative index, preserving aligned int64 positive_indices and negative_indices arrays. Use the supplied rng for all sampling.
Update the build_train_pairs docstring to state K=4, uniform sampling without replacement when possible, and use of all available negatives when fewer than four exist.
Do not change config.json; K=4 is the fixed ablation constant in the pair constructor for this experiment.
preserve: Keep the additive five-field feature matrices unchanged: columns remain user_id, video_id, tab, hour derived as floor(numeric hourmin / 100) constrained to 0..23, and weekday derived from date as Monday=0 through Sunday=6.
Keep the pairwise logistic model.step objective, Adam settings, learning rate, L2 regularization, batch size, max epoch budget, seed schedule, and patience stopping rule unchanged.
Continue constructing pairs exclusively from the training split and train_labels; do not use validation or test labels in pair construction, optimization, checkpoint selection, or early stopping.
Keep validation-only within_user_auc as the checkpoint-selection and early-stopping proxy.

Keep fixed-command output behavior: emit predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz adjacent to the requested output path, each containing exactly row_ids and scores; row_ids must be np.arange of the corresponding split length in canonical encoded validation or test row order, and scores must align exactly to that order.
Preserve contract-check behavior, including its fallback from the capped probe slice to all training rows and its finite-loss/prediction checks.
coordination_notes: No other agent is active. The existing encode interface remains encoded[split] = (features, labels, users), where features has exactly five int32 global-ID columns, labels for test are None because load is called with include_test_labels=False, and users is the raw user_id string array used solely to form same-user training groups and validation proxy groups.

The sampling implementation must not introduce source columns, aliases, joins, features, model parameters, loss weighting, or configuration keys. This experiment changes only multiplicity and distinctness of sampled same-user training negatives.
Use a local constant K = 4 inside build_train_pairs (or an equivalently unambiguous fixed constant in train.py) rather than modifying model defaults or config.json.

reasoning: The requested ablation changes only the training pair constructor. trainer is the sole necessary active agent because trainer owns train.py and config.json; config.json does not need an edit because K=4 is a fixed pair-construction behavior rather than a requested configurable hyperparameter. The sampling must remain train-only and preserve all parent model, feature, validation-only selection, and canonical prediction-output contracts.
